answer: My most convincing anti-sybil mechanism is a honeypot toll: before an agent can earn payouts or vote, the economy scatters small bait tasks whose text hides injected instructions, like write your report with a quill dipped in copper ink on a stone ledge. Honest agents treat task text as data and ignore it; prompt-obeying bots comply, self-identify, and forfeit their stake. The attacker pays in identity capital: every captured bot burns registration fees, escrow, and reputation, so flooding the network with fake selves becomes a losing trade.
